title: Efficiency
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between useful and total energy?
If a machine is not 100 percent efficient, what does that mean?
How can we calculate the percentage efficiency for a simple circuit?

explain.say: Today we learn about efficiency in machines. Efficiency tells us how well a machine works. It compares useful energy to the total energy used.
The useful energy is the part that actually performs the job. The total energy is everything that goes into the machine system. Think of it like the starting fuel.
We calculate efficiency using a simple formula. It is useful energy divided by total energy. We then multiply by one hundred to get a percentage.
For example, if a motor uses one hundred joules. And it does one hundred minus ten joules of useful work. The efficiency is ninety percent.
In real life, think about a car engine. The total energy comes from the fuel burned. The useful energy is the energy that moves the car forward.
A common mistake is forgetting to multiply by one hundred. If you just divide the numbers, you will get a decimal, not a percentage. Always remember the final step.

items: The final answer must be a percentage.

draw.text: Do not forget to multiply by 100!

faq.q: What does it mean if a machine has an efficiency of zero percent?
faq.a: It means that none of the energy put into the machine is doing any useful work. All the energy is lost as heat or sound.
asks: Can a machine have zero efficiency?
What happens if efficiency is zero?

faq.q: Is it possible for an efficiency to be greater than one hundred percent?
faq.a: No, it is not possible for an efficiency to be over one hundred percent. This would mean the machine is creating energy from nothing, which violates physics laws.
asks: Is it possible to gain energy?

faq.q: What is the energy that gets wasted in a machine?
faq.a: Wasted energy usually appears as heat or sound. These forms of energy are still present but are not used for the machine's intended purpose.
asks: Where does the lost energy go?
What is wasted energy in physics?

faq.q: Do we need to use joules or watts when calculating efficiency?
faq.a: We must use the same unit for both useful and total energy, such as joules. Efficiency is a ratio, so the units cancel out.
asks: Does the unit matter for efficiency?

faq.q: How can I improve the efficiency of a machine?
faq.a: You can improve efficiency by reducing sources of energy loss, such as friction or air resistance. Better design helps minimize waste.
asks: How to make a machine more efficient?

facts: Efficiency is a ratio comparing useful energy to total energy.
The formula for efficiency is (Useful Energy / Total Energy) x 100.
Energy is often wasted as heat or sound when machines operate.
Efficiency can never be greater than one hundred percent.

quiz.say: A machine uses one hundred joules of energy and produces thirty joules of useful work. What is its efficiency?
quiz.why: The efficiency is calculated by dividing the useful energy (thirty joules) by the total energy (one hundred joules) and multiplying by one hundred. Thirty divided by one hundred is zero point three, which is thirty percent.

wrong.0: This assumes no energy is wasted, which is usually not the case.
wrong.1: This is the correct ratio, but the question asks for a percentage.
wrong.3: This is the percentage of wasted energy, not the useful energy percentage.

quiz.say: If a light bulb uses sixty watts of power and outputs forty watts of visible light, what is its efficiency?
quiz.why: Efficiency is forty watts divided by sixty watts, multiplied by one hundred. This gives approximately sixty-six point seven percent.

wrong.0: This incorrectly calculates the ratio by dividing the total by the useful energy.
wrong.2: This is the correct ratio, but the question asks for a percentage.
wrong.3: This only uses the useful energy and ignores the total energy input.

quiz.say: A simple pulley system requires one hundred joules of input energy to lift a box. If the box is lifted using only eighty joules of useful energy, what is the efficiency?
quiz.why: The efficiency is found by dividing the useful energy, eighty joules, by the total energy, one hundred joules, and multiplying by one hundred. This results in eighty percent.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the two energy values together.
wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that all the input energy was useful.
wrong.3: This calculates the wasted energy percentage, not the useful energy percentage.
